name: @stonedogcode/release-notes
description: A release-notes surface for applications: releases described by their deploys, filtered to what a customer should read, grouped by day, with an optional what's-new prompt and a host-configured way to report a problem.
author: StoneDogCode L.L.C.
//exports: Ships TypeScript SOURCE rather than a bundle so a consumer compiles it with its own tsconfig and bundler. NOTE: unlike @stonedogcode/style and @stonedogcode/howto, this package depends on NO design system — the components emit semantic HTML with stable class names and accept a `components` override map. Four products style themselves differently, and importing one of their systems here would make the package unusable by the other three. So there is no Panda `include` glob to configure.
//files: The __tests__ exclusion is load-bearing, not tidiness. Consumers add `node_modules/@stonedogcode/release-notes/src/**` to their Panda `include` globs, so anything shipped under src/ is statically parsed at THEIR build — and the tests import jest globals and fixture data. They also ship a test suite nobody can run to every consumer.

scripts.//test: Jest runs as ESM (see jest.config.cjs), which needs the VM modules flag.
scripts.gate: npm run type-check && npm run lint && npm run test && npm run verify:package

//peerDependencies: Only the `./node` subpath needs @types/node, and only for TYPE-CHECKING — we ship TypeScript source rather than a bundle, so the consumer's tsc compiles our `node:fs` import itself. Optional, because a consumer using only the main entry point needs nothing. Found by verify-package.sh on its first run against the subpath: the throwaway consumer failed with `Cannot find module 'node:fs'`, which is invisible to a test suite running inside this repo where @types/node is a devDependency.
//peerDependenciesMeta: Both optional. @types/node is needed only to TYPE-CHECK the ./node subpath; react only if you import the components. A host using just the pure core (publicReleases, groupReleasesByDay, whatsNew) needs neither.
